Discrimination of an internally derived routine CT score was evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: Of 328 patients, 161 (49.1%) were smear positive. Cavity prevalence increased from 29.9% in smear-negative patients to 80.0% in grade 3+ smears, and median CT extent from 19.0% to 34.5%. An extent ≥25% (odds ratio [OR]: 3.05, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.80-5.15), cavity (OR: 2.92, 1.77-4.82), and consolidation (OR: 2.19, 1.32-3.63) were independently associated with smear positivity and higher smear grade (ORs: 3.71, 3.44, and 2.72, respectively). The CT score showed moderate discrimination (AUC: 0.765). Sensitivity analyses were directionally consistent. CONCLUSION: Greater CT extent, cavitation, and consolidation were independently associated with smear positivity and higher grade. These findings support CT features as correlates of smear burden but do not establish a role for CT-directed isolation or microbiologic prioritisation.

articles.title: Multiparametric 0.4-T low-field MRI mapping for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in rats.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Low-field MRI may broaden access to quantitative liver imaging, but low signal-to-noise ratio and coexisting steatosis, inflammation, fibrosis, and iron complicate relaxometry in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We evaluated multiparametric 0.4-T MRI with deep-learning-reconstructed T1 mapping in rats. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective cross-sectional preclinical study, 90 male Wistar rats underwent 0.4-T liver MRI during dietary induction, progression, and recovery. Metrics included native T1, fat-corrected T1 (FcT1), T2, T2*, and an apparent proton density fat fraction (PDFF) estimate. Whole-section digital pathology quantified steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation, and iron. Associations were assessed using iron-adjusted and stage-aware analyses, multivariable regression with variance inflation factors, and receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: Steatosis strongly correlated with T2 (ρ = 0.90, p < 0.001) and PDFF (ρ = 0.88, p < 0.001). For high inflammation, T2 and T2* yielded areas under the curve (AUROCs) of 0.86 (95% confidence interval 0.78-0.94) and 0.80 (0.71-0.89), respectively (p = 0.294); specificities were 82.2% and 91.1%, respectively. For fibrosis, native T1 yielded higher AUROCs than FcT1 at collagen proportionate area (CPA) > 2.42% (0.77 versus 0.62; p = 0.008) and > 2.90% (0.78 versus 0.60; p = 0.001). Stage-aware analyses attenuated T1-fibrosis associations, and recovery animals showed residual fibrosis with near-baseline T1. CONCLUSION: Multiparametric 0.4-T MRI showed complementary, partly stage-dependent associations with MASLD pathology. T2/PDFF tracked steatosis; T2* retained an inflammation-related association after stage adjustment; and T1 elevation characterized active high-burden progression rather than isolated residual fibrosis. Human validation and platform calibration are required. KEY POINTS: Question Noninvasive MASLD assessment needs accessible imaging biomarkers that account for coexisting steatosis, inflammation, fibrosis, and iron-related confounding in liver MRI. Findings Multiparametric 0.4-T MRI showed complementary but stage-dependent associations: T2/apparent PDFF tracked steatosis, T2* related to inflammation, and T1 rose during high-burden progression. Relevance statement Multiparametric 0.4-T MRI provides complementary pathology-correlated measurements for MASLD assessment in rats, but reconstruction-dependent T1 bias and apparent PDFF estimation require platform calibration and human validation before clinical interpretation.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy and reliability of susceptibility map-weighted imaging in patients with clinically uncertain parkinsonian syndromes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, accompanied by increased iron accumulation, particularly in the nigrosome-1 subregion. Differentiating neurodegenerative disorders like PD from non-neurodegenerative causes of parkinsonism can be challenging. In clinically uncertain parkinsonian syndrome (CUPS), dopamine transporter (DAT)-single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) can aid diagnosis. However, susceptibility map-weighted imaging (SMWI) provides a promising magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alternative. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and reliability of visual SMWI assessment by radiologists in CUPS and the added value of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic software. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with CUPS who underwent DAT-SPECT between January 2019 and July 2023 were included. Four radiologists, blinded to clinical symptoms and diagnosis, visually rated nigrosome-1 on axial SMWI reconstructions as normal, unclear, or abnormal. After the initial assessment, the radiologists re-evaluated the scans with AI-driven software assistance, designed to classify and quantify nigrosome-1 integrity. The reference standard was the final clinical diagnosis incorporating DAT-SPECT results. RESULTS: One hundred eighty patients were included (mean age 67.9, range 31-86, 120 males), 84 with neurodegenerative and 96 with non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism. Mean diagnostic accuracy was 80% (range 73-83%), with substantial inter-rater reliability (Fleiss κ 0.65). With software assistance, diagnostic accuracy improved to 87% (range 85-91%), and inter-rater agreement increased to almost perfect (Fleiss κ 0.86). CONCLUSION: SMWI, particularly with AI-driven software assistance, is a promising and accessible MRI-based technique that may support the diagnostic workup in clinically uncertain parkinsonism, aiding the distinction between neurodegenerative and non-neurodegenerative causes. KEY POINTS: Question Can susceptibility map-weighted imaging (SMWI) reliably differentiate neurodegenerative from non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism in clinically uncertain cases, and does artificial intelligence (AI)-driven software assistance improve radiologist performance? Findings Visual assessment had an accuracy of 80%, with substantial inter-rater reliability. AI-driven software assistance increased accuracy to 87% and improved inter-rater reliability. Relevance statement SMWI can differentiate neurodegenerative from non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism in clinically uncertain cases and may support the diagnostic process by offering an accessible MRI-based technique, facilitating an efficient diagnostic workup, and enabling early diagnosis in clinically uncertain parkinsonism.

articles.title: Tensor-based dynamic MRI reconstruction with non-convex ℓrp pseudo-norm and adaptive weighting.
articles.abstract: Compressed sensing significantly accelerates dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) by undersampling (k, t)-space, thereby formulating an ill-posed inverse problem that heavily depends on reconstruction algorithms. Dynamic MRI data exhibit low-rank property due to strong correlations in both spatial and temporal dimensions. In this paper, we propose a tensor-based ℓrp pseudo-norm regularization for low-rank dynamic MRI reconstruction model, and introduce the weighting mechanism to adaptively distinguish between signal and noise, termed as TNWLR. We take tensor as processing unit to protect the inherent structure and facilitate the exploitation of its inherent structural correlations. The utilization of tensor-based ℓrp pseudo-norm adequately exploits the spatial and temporal redundancies, and provides a flexible non-convex approximation to the rank function. In addition, using the weighting mechanism enables the suppression of noise and artifacts while better preserving the low-rank structure. The alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM) provides an efficient solution framework for the proposed model due to its ability to decouple complex constraints. Compared with representative reconstruction methods, extensive experiments on multi-coil brain and liver DCE-MRI datasets demonstrate improved quantitative performance and better visual preservation of anatomical structures and fine details, and strong robustness to noise.

articles.title: The impaired white matter integrity and altered functional connectivity in Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by structural abnormalities in the cerebral cortex and subcortical regions. Nevertheless, functional connectivity (FC) alterations within these affected white matter (WM) regions have not been fully clarified. METHODS: We combine diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) to explore abnormalities in WM structure and FC in 20 PD patients and 22 age- and gender-matched healthy controls (HCs). RESULTS: Compared with the HCs, PD patients showed lower fractional anisotropy (FA) values in multiple widespread WM tracts, including the the forceps minor, the bilateral inferior longitudinal fasciculus, the right inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus, corticospinal tract (CST) and superior longitudinal fasciculus (SLF), the left anterior thalamic radiation (ATR), uncinate fasciculus and cingulum. Seed-based FC analysis revealed that: for the CST seed, PD patients exhibited reduced FC with the bilateral postcentral gyrus and precentral gyrus, the right superior occipital gyrus and left inferior parietal lobule. For the SLF seed, PD patients exhibited reduced FC with the bilateral anterior cingulate cortex. For the ATR seed, hypoconnectivity was found in multiple cerebellar subregions, including the bilateral cerebellum VIII and cerebellum IX, the right cerebellum VI and cerebellar crus I, and the left middle temporal gyrus. CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that PD patients exhibit widespread WM microstructural damage and some of these damaged fibers show abnormal FC, which may account for motor deficits and cognitive decline observed in PD. The combined use of DTI and rs-fMRI provides novel perspectives on the neural mechanisms underlying PD.
